transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Bridgewater Head of ML), Priya Singh (Bridgewater Platform Eng), Daniel Gomez (CTO), Sofia Alvarez (DevOps)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be noisy): Bridgewater wants more capacity and regions. Discuss pricing for committed pool, benchmarks to validate latency/cost tradeoffs, security docs requested.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i guess we can kick off — Ethan and I will run through capacity and next steps.
[00:12] Ethan Park: hi all, Ethan here, SE. we'll talk about the dedicated upgrade plan and what the benchmark will look like.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: thanks, quick note, we're tight on time next week so wanted to confirm options before legal loops.
[00:30] Priya Singh: yes, and we have questions about data residency, KMS, and if you support private HSM, i think that's important.
[00:40] Maya Chen: great, exactly why we scheduled this. quick agenda: current usage review, proposed 10-GPU pool + regions, pricing and term, security checklist, and bench plan. sound good?
[00:52] Daniel Gomez: yep
[00:55] Sofia Alvarez: yep good

[01:05] Ethan Park: quick baseline — you're currently on a 4-GPU dedicated pool in us-west, right? we see steady 1300 qps peaks for your batch inference and some spikes to 2k qps during end-of-month runs.
[01:22] Liam O'Connor: that's right. also we're rolling more features and expect steady 30% growth next quarter.
[01:28] Maya Chen: ok natural fit for increasing to a 10-GPU reserved capacity, that gives headroom and allows for burst configs. we can do a hybrid: committed 8 GPUs + 2 burst on demand, or full 10 committed which affects unit price.
[01:44] Priya Singh: what's the expected latency delta if we go to EU region? our EU customers need sub-120ms for tail p95.
[01:52] Ethan Park: good q. for EU region we typically see p95 of ~80-110ms for models in your catalog with our optimized kernels — depends on sequence length and KV cache hit rate. one caveat, our KV cache sometimes appears in transcript as KV cash in older docs — sorry that's a little joke — but real point is prefix caching will help your tail latency.
[02:15] Liam O'Connor: haha noted. also, do you support VPC peering into eu-west? our security team requires private networking.
[02:22] Maya Chen: yes, VPC peering is supported — private control plane option. we'll share the onboarding checklist; KMS integration with BYOK and HSM options are available (Ethan: correct me if i'm wrong).
[02:33] Ethan Park: correct, we support KMS + customer-managed keys, and for on-prem we have deployment packages. note: some customers call Kubernetes "kubeernetes" in notes — transcription. for compliance there's a SOC 2 package we can send.

[03:00] Priya Singh: legal also asked about data at rest encryption and audit logs retention for 7 years — is that something Redwood handles or add-on?
[03:08] Maya Chen: audit logs are part of our enterprise package; long-term retention is an add-on. we'll include retention pricing.

[03:20] Daniel Gomez: switching to pricing, what kind of discount do we get with a 12-month extension for 10 committed GPUs? we currently have a 6-month rolling.
[03:30] Maya Chen: for a 12-month commit on 10 GPUs we'd propose a tiered discount — roughly 18-25% off base unit price depending on burst allowance and support SLA. i'll put exact numbers in a spreadsheet.
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: would you do a runway where we start with 8 committed then add 2 after benchmark results?
[03:46] Ethan Park: that's the recommended pattern — 8 committed gives immediate cost-savings and 2 on-demand gives safety. then after bench we can commit to full 10.

[04:02] Priya Singh: on benchmarking, what will you need from our side?
[04:06] Ethan Park: ideally a representative traffic CSV, model checkpoints if you're using custom fine-tuned weights, and expected sequence length distribution. we'll run both throughput and tail-latency tests across US/EU and optionally APAC.
[04:20] Priya Singh: we can share the traffic CSV by Tuesday. note: some fields may have PII, we should sanitize.
[04:27] Maya Chen: yes please sanitize. we'll provide a secure upload link.

[04:40] Sofia Alvarez: operational question — what's the lead time for provisioning a new EU region pool and VPC peering?
[04:46] Ethan Park: typically 7-10 business days for provisioning and peering, if nothing custom. if you require dedicated peering windows and our infra team needs change control it can be 2-3 weeks.
[04:58] Daniel Gomez: ok that fits our timeline if we sign by mid-July.

[05:08] Liam O'Connor: is there any risk of failing audits with your SOC2 docs? our security folks will do an internal gap.
[05:13] Maya Chen: SOC2 is standard; we'll send the report and a controls mapping. if you need ISO or specific certifications for APAC we can discuss roadmap.

[05:30] Priya Singh: about cost — what's the cost per 1M tokens at 10 GPUs? i know it varies but ballpark.
[05:38] Maya Chen: it depends on batching and cache hit rate. rough ballpark with optimized batching and quantization: $X per 1M tokens at committed rate — i'll put concrete numbers in the pricing sheet.
[05:50] Ethan Park: also note quality tradeoffs with quantization, we usually recommend model-specific quant profiles. we can run evals to compare.

[06:10] Daniel Gomez: competitors: we've seen Bedrock offers managed endpoint with lower overhead, and Replicate for simpler infra. why Redwood vs those?
[06:20] Maya Chen: main diffs: production-first runtime and consistent controls across hosted/dedicated/private, plus tooling for rollouts and cost controls. we also have model/quant recommendations tied to your workload to avoid blind quality regressions.
[06:35] Liam O'Connor: good.

[06:40] Ethan Park: quick technical note — for our bench we'll use continuous batching and KV cache priming to emulate real traffic. we ask you for sample prefixes to warm the cache. if not available we use synthetic.
[06:55] Priya Singh: ok will share prefixes.

[07:05] Maya Chen: timeline recap: Maya sends pricing and contract options by 2026-07-01, Bridgewater shares traffic and prefixes by 2026-06-30, Ethan runs bench week of 2026-07-06 and shares results.
[07:20] Daniel Gomez: and legal review sits after we get pricing — probably two weeks.

[07:30] Sofia Alvarez: one more question — fallback when capacity saturates, do you support automatic fallback to hosted model or auto-scaling?
[07:36] Ethan Park: yes we support policy-based routing: you can route to hosted fallback, or to a cheaper quantized variant, or to another region. autoscaling is configurable but reserved capacity doesn't autoscale beyond burst configuration.
[07:52] Priya Singh: what's the burst billback model? we prefer predictable bills.
[07:57] Maya Chen: burst usage is billed at on-demand rates; we can model scenarios in the pricing sheet and show monthly variance projections.

[08:12] Liam O'Connor: any gotchas about migrating from our current 4-GPU to 10-GPU dedicated?
[08:17] Ethan Park: main items: model compatibility with quantization, checkpoint formats, and KV cache priming. also make sure you pin model versions for rollout safety.
[08:28] Priya Singh: we have a custom tokenizer — any issues?
[08:31] Ethan Park: we can host your tokenizer as part of the deployment; might need a quick packaging step.

[08:42] Maya Chen: ok i'll attach packaging docs.

[09:00] (brief cross-talk while people check calendars)
[09:15] Maya Chen: any other blockers?
[09:17] Daniel Gomez: main blocker is legal on data residency and the final price.
[09:21] Priya Singh: also need the SOC2 mapping.
[09:23] Maya Chen: noted, we'll send that.

[09:30] Ethan Park: one last thing — APAC region: we can stand up a small warm pool (2 GPUs) for latency-sensitive users as a follow-on after EU bench. provisioning for APAC is usually 10-14 days.
[09:45] Liam O'Connor: sounds good, maybe after we see EU numbers.

[10:00] Maya Chen: cool. recap of Owners and next steps: Maya — pricing and contract options; Ethan — bench config; Bridgewater (Liam/Priya/Sofia) — test data and peering windows.
[10:14] Priya Singh: we'll get the CSV and the peering windows.
[10:18] Daniel Gomez: thanks, Maya and Ethan.
[10:21] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, talk soon.

[end of transcript]
